findings.finding: Last resource checkpoint runs during worker polling. After TERM/KILL/reap, scratch is deleted without a final scratch/free observation; result and budget are then written without a post-write resource/deadline observation. A terminal spike during cleanup or final writes can be erased from evidence and still yield PASS. sizes also silently ignores os.walk scandir errors.
findings.requestedFix: Reuse narrow non-deadline resource observation before scratch removal and after evidence writes, explicit non-ENOENT scan-error propagation, actual final timing evidence and failure retention while safe owned cleanup continues. Avoid a new general runner framework.

findings.finding: Worker is started in a new session but parent has no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler. Normal SIGTERM terminates Python without entering finally, leaving its separate worker/Chrome group outside the parent cleanup path and budget incomplete. SIGKILL remains unhandleable, but ordinary cooperative stops are handleable.
findings.requestedFix: Install a narrow cooperative stop flag/handlers before launch; let the same finally terminate/reap the owned group and persist failure. Restore handlers after cleanup. Do not claim immunity to SIGKILL or inspect unrelated processes.
